subject: Post-call: Logging sanitization scope & SLA checkpoints
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medsys.health>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Security Ops <sec-ops@medsys.health>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:15:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-call: Logging sanitization scope & SLA checkpoints

Thanks Rishi — quick follow-up from our call this morning. A couple of clarifications so we can get requirements into the procurement worksheet:  

1) Scope of data we need removed/masked from request/response logs: email addresses, phone numbers, SSNs (when they appear), and any free-text PII found in the request body. We want automated redaction that is configurable per route.
2) Trace IDs: we need correlation across systems. Hashing is acceptable but it must be deterministic (same input -> same hash) and irreversible for privacy. Can Redwood provide a salted hash option and document the salt management?
3) Retention windows: short-term request logs (30 days) and long-term audit exports (up to 365 days) with distinct retention policies. Can logs be kept in an EU region only?
4) Evidence: SOC2 and data flow diagram needed for our legal/compliance review.

If you can confirm these items and send a short technical runbook that shows how Redwood would implement per-route masking + the options for trace-id hashing and regional log residency, we can move the procurement team to draft an SOW.

Best,
Alex
Alex Torres
Head of InfoSec, MedSys Health

Subject: Re: Post-call: Logging sanitization scope & SLA checkpoints

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below are Redwood's baseline answers and the proposed next steps. I'm copying Monica (Solutions Engineering) to scope the technical runbook and Marissa (Privacy & Compliance) for evidence.

Summary (short):
- Per-route masking: supported via route config. We offer token-level redaction rules (regex + ML PII detector) that run pre-ingest; rules are policy-specified per-customer and per-route.
- Trace ID handling: we support deterministic HMAC-SHA256 hashing with customer-provided KMS key or Redwood-managed salt (we can provide both options). Deterministic hashing preserves correlation while preventing raw trace exposure.
- Retention & residency: logs can be sharded by region. For EU-only residency we will pin log storage to eu-west-1 and ensure no replication outside region for the dataset. Retention policies are configurable per-log type (request logs vs audit exports).
- Evidence: attaching a short summary PDF (redwood-logging-options-summary.pdf) that maps features to your asks. SOC2 report and architecture diagram are available — Marissa will share the latest copies under NDA if needed.

Proposed next steps & owners:
1) Monica to produce the technical runbook (per-route config examples, sample regex/ML rules, HMAC setup). ETA: 3 business days.
2) Marissa to add SOC2 + architecture diagram to the secure share. ETA: 1 business day (pending NDA).
3) Follow-up technical call (MedSys SecOps + Monica) to walk the runbook and agree on masking rules. Propose: Thu 6 May, 14:00 CEST.
4) Procurement worksheet: once runbook + evidence posted, Alex to confirm retention windows for each log type so we can populate SOW.

Attachments: redwood-logging-options-summary.pdf (feature mapping), medsys-maP-requirements.xlsx (your worksheet template, lightly annotated).

If that plan looks good, Monica — can you own the runbook and confirm availability for Thu 6 May 14:00 CEST?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Logging sanitization scope & SLA checkpoints

Alex — Monica here. Thanks for the checklist. I attached a technical runbook draft to the Drive link in the HubSpot note (see related_links). High-level responses to your asks:  

- PII masking: we recommend a two-layer approach — (1) deterministic regex/PII models at pre-ingest to redact known patterns (emails, phones, SSNs); (2) probabilistic model for free-text PII with thresholding and human-in-the-loop review for edge cases. The runbook includes sample regex rules and example per-route YAML for enabling/disabling detectors.
- Trace IDs: we will implement deterministic HMAC with a customer-specified KMS key. We document key rotation behavior: rotating the KMS key will change future hash outputs; we can preserve a rolling mapping for a configurable window if you need cross-period correlation.
- Retention & residency: confirming we can pin both raw and redacted logs to eu-west-1. Request logs -> 30 days by default (configurable). Audit exports -> configurable up to 365 days. We provide export hooks for your SIEM.
- Evidence: Marissa will drop SOC2 Type II and the architecture diagram into a secure share after NDA is recorded.

Next steps (concrete):
1) I'll run the technical call on Thu 6 May 14:00 CEST. Calendar invite sent to Alex and SecOps.
2) I'll drop the runbook draft and a small test plan (sample inputs + expected redacted outputs) to the secure folder. Please attach a small set of representative payloads (anonymized) to validate rules.
3) After validation, we'll provide a short config artifact that you can include in the SOW (masking toggles, retention numbers, residency confirmation, trace-id HMAC option).

Let me know if you want deterministic hashing to be performed via your KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed salt. If you choose KMS, include the key ARN in the secure share and we'll schedule a short key onboarding call.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
